overall: Los Angeles is experiencing classic June Gloom conditions early this morning, with temperatures locked at 62.6°F since midnight and zero warming velocity — the marine layer is firmly in place with patchy fog and mostly cloudy skies. The overnight temperature has been remarkably flat (62.1–62.6°F across all observations), indicating a persistent onshore flow and suppressed boundary layer. The day is expected to follow a typical marine-layer burn-off pattern, with meaningful warming not occurring until late morning or early afternoon.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show solid agreement, clustering tightly between 67.0°F (NBM) and 69.8°F (HRRR), with ECMWF at 68.2°F — a spread of under 3°F, which is reassuring. The NWS official forecast of 69°F aligns well with this consensus. Peak timing models (mean 17.0h ET, or ~2 PM PT) are consistent and plausible given the fog burn-off timeline, though the intraday model's early 14.5h ET peak signal reflects the lack of morning warming data rather than a true early peak.
max_temp_prediction: Given the tight NWP model consensus of 67–70°F and NWS forecast of 69°F, the most likely TMAX is in the upper 60s, with 68–69°F as the central estimate. The lingering marine layer and mostly cloudy sky through late morning slightly cap upside risk, arguing for landing near or just below the HRRR's 69.8°F rather than above it. Confidence is moderate-to-high for the 67–71°F range; the active alerts (Red Flag, Extreme Heat) all apply to inland desert areas well removed from coastal LA and pose no meaningful upside risk for today's high.
